title: Quicksort Partition

description.intro:
Given an array of integers, arr, and an integer, pivot, modify arr in place using only O(1) extra space so that (1) every element smaller than the pivot appears before every element greater than or equal to the pivot, and (2) every element larger than the pivot appears after every element smaller than or equal to the pivot.

The relative order of the elements smaller than or greater than the pivot does not matter.
examples:
Example 1:
Input: arr = [1, 7, 2, 3, 3, 5, 3], pivot = 4
Output: [1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 7, 5]
Explanation: The array is partitioned into:

- Elements less than 4: [1, 2, 3, 3, 3]
- Elements equal to 4: []
- Elements greater than 4: [7, 5]
  Other orders, such as [3, 2, 1, 3, 3, 5, 7], would also be valid.

Example 2:
Input: arr = [1, 7, 2, 3, 3, 5, 3], pivot = 3
Output: [1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 7, 5]
Explanation: The array is partitioned into:

- Elements less than 3: [1, 2]
- Elements equal to 3: [3, 3, 3]
- Elements greater than 3: [7, 5]
  Other orders, such as [2, 1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 7], would also be valid.
  Constraints:
We can use the inward pointers movement pattern to solve this problem.
The idea is to have two pointers, l and r, moving in opposite directions, and swapping pairs of elements in the wrong side of the partition. The challenge is where to put elements equal to the pivot.
One approach is to use the break down the problem booster to solve it in two steps:

Put all the elements <= pivot before all the elements > pivot
Now, take the section of the array with the elements <= pivot and use inward pointers again to put the elements < pivot before those = pivot
This is a two-pass solution, but it doesn't change the runtime analysis. Each pass takes O(n) time, where n is the size of the array, so the total runtime is O(n).

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n: the length of the array

Time: O(n) - the algorithm makes two passes through the array

Extra space: O(1) - the partitioning is done in-place using only constant extra space for the pointers
